title: Reactance, impedance and resonance
blurb: Explain how coils and capacitors oppose AC, what impedance is, and why XL equals XC at resonance.

G5A01.why: At resonance XL = XC and they cancel, so a series LC circuit has very **low** impedance.
G5A01.trap: A parallel LC circuit is the reverse; the series one is low. Neither uses a mean of L and C.

G5A02.why: Reactance is opposition to **alternating** current from capacitance or inductance. Resistance opposes any current.
G5A02.trap: Opposition from resistance is just resistance. Nothing here reinforces current.

G5A03.trap: Reluctance is magnetic. Conductance and admittance are inverses.

G5A04.trap: Reluctance is magnetic. Conductance and admittance are inverses.

G5A05.why: An inductor's reactance **rises** with frequency: XL = 2π × f × L.
G5A05.trap: Amplitude does not change reactance. Falling reactance with frequency is the capacitor.

G5A06.why: A capacitor's reactance **falls** as frequency rises: XC = 1 ÷ (2π × f × C).
G5A06.trap: Rising reactance with frequency is the inductor. Amplitude is irrelevant.

G5A07.why: Admittance is the **inverse of impedance**: Y = 1 ÷ Z.
G5A07.trap: Conductance is the inverse of resistance, susceptance of reactance.

G5A08.why: Impedance is **voltage ÷ current**, Z = E ÷ I, the AC form of Ohm's law.
G5A08.trap: Current over voltage is the inverse (admittance). Volts times amperes is power.

G5A09.why: Reactance is opposition, so it is measured in **ohms**, like resistance and impedance.
G5A09.trap: Farad is capacitance, ampere is current, siemens is conductance.

G5A10.why: A transformer, a Pi-network and a length of transmission line can **all** transform impedances.

G5A11.why: Reactance is **X** (XL, XC). Z is impedance, R is resistance.
G5A11.trap: Z is impedance. B and Y are susceptance and admittance.

G5A12.why: At resonance **XL and XC are equal and cancel**, leaving only the resistance.
G5A12.trap: Resistance never cancels. Resonant circuits keep their energy; they do not radiate it all.
